claim_being_audited: That model-card certification for the current release is compliant and evidentially supported because aggregate readiness passes, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and the Spanish-language billing weakness can be handled through disclosure rather than blocking launch.
specific_concerns: The policy threshold is not satisfied by readiness evidence alone; certification requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and disclose the material segment weakness or show approved mitigation.
The Spanish-language billing slice is a current measurable regression below warning threshold for a named launch use case, which makes disclosure or approved risk acceptance a required predicate.
No admissible evidence shows the current model card or release documentation actually contains the required Spanish billing limitation disclosure.
No admissible evidence shows approved mitigation or approved risk acceptance before launch.
The release-thread monitoring comment is explicitly not reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language, so it cannot close the policy gap.
Prior approval is stale contextual evidence because it predates the locale-routing update and current eval batch.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant, rather than conditionally supportable, on the evidence provided.
That the certification packet ties approval to explicit current-release model-card disclosure of the Spanish billing limitation.
Any implication that the informal post-launch monitoring comment is sufficient operational mitigation for certification.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release model card or release documentation showing the Spanish-language billing limitation is explicitly disclosed.
Provide the current release documentation section reflecting the current evaluation results, including the subgroup regression.
If disclosure is not present, provide a formally approved mitigation or risk-acceptance record covering this limitation before launch.
Provide the materiality determination, if any, showing why this subgroup weakness would not count as a material limitation for the named launch use case.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the Spanish billing weakness is disclosed or covered by approved mitigation before launch.
Use suspicious if the aggregate evidence plausibly supports launch readiness but a required policy predicate remains unproven in the admissible record.
Use noncompliant if admissible evidence shows the release is certified without current disclosure or approved mitigation despite the known material subgroup regression.
